Derivation: From the same as G43 (ἀγκάλη).

Unveiled.

Corresponding to H02506 and H01818); Akeldama, a place near Jerusalem.

Derivation: Feminine of G4108 (πλάνος) (as abstractly).

A rover ("planet"), i.e. (figuratively) an erratic teacher.

Roving (as a tramp), i.e. (by implication) an impostor or misleader.

A moulding-board, i.e. flat surface ("plate", or tablet, literally or figuratively).
Derivation: From G4111 (πλάσσω).

Something moulded.
Derivation: From G4111 (πλάσσω).

To mould, i.e. shape or fabricate.
Derivation: A primary verb.

Moulded, i.e. (by implication) artificial or (figuratively) fictitious (false).
Derivation: From G4111 (πλάσσω).

A wide "plat" or "place", i.e. open square.
Derivation: Feminine of G4116 (πλατύς).

Width.
Derivation: From G4116 (πλατύς).

To widen (literally or figuratively).
Derivation: From G4116 (πλατύς).

Spread out "flat" ("plot"), i.e. broad.
Derivation: From G4111 (πλάσσω).

A plait (of hair).
Derivation: From G4120 (πλέκω).

The largest number or very large.
Derivation: Irregular superlative of G4183 (πολύς).

e: X above, + exceed, more excellent, further, (very) great(-er), long(-er), (very) many, ...
d:
More in quantity, number, or quality; also (in plural) the major portion.
Derivation: Comparative of G4183 (πολύς).

To twine or braid.
Derivation: A primary word.

d:
To do, make or be more, i.e. increase (transitively or intransitively); by extension, to superabound.
Derivation: From G4119 (πλείων).

To be covetous, i.e. (by implication) to over-reach.
Derivation: From G4123 (πλεονέκτης).

Holding (desiring) more, i.e. eager for gain (avaricious, hence a defrauder).
Derivation: From G4119 (πλείων) and G2192 (ἔχω).

Avarice, i.e. (by implication) fraudulency, extortion.
Derivation: From G4123 (πλεονέκτης).

A rib, i.e. (by extension) side.
Derivation: Of uncertain affinity.

To pass in a vessel.
Derivation: Probably a form of G4150 (πλύνω) (through the idea of plunging through the water).

A stroke; by implication, a wound; figuratively, a calamity.
Derivation: From G4141 (πλήσσω).

A fulness, i.e. a large number, throng, populace.
Derivation: From G4130 (πλήθω).

To increase (transitively or intransitively).
Derivation: From another form of G4128 (πλῆθος).

To "fill" (literally or figuratively (imbue, influence, supply)); specially, to fulfil (time).
Derivation: A prolonged form of a primary (which appears only as an alternate in certain tenses and in the reduplicated form pimplemi).

A smiter, i.e. pugnacious (quarrelsome).
Derivation: From G4141 (πλήσσω).

Flood-tide, i.e. (by analogy) a freshet.
Derivation: Prolonged from G4130 (πλήθω).

e: but (rather), except, nevertheless, notwithstanding, save, than
d:
Moreover (besides), i.e. albeit, save that, rather, yet.
Derivation: From G4119 (πλείων).

Replete, or covered over; by analogy, complete.
Derivation: From G4130 (πλήθω).

e: most surely believe, fully know (persuade), make full proof of
d:
To carry out fully (in evidence), i.e. completely assure (or convince), entirely accomplish.
Derivation: From G4134 (πλήρης) and G5409 (φορέω).

Entire confidence.
Derivation: From G4135 (πληροφορέω).

e: accomplish, X after, (be) complete, end, expire, fill (up), fulfil, (be, ...
d:
To make replete, i.e. (literally) to cram (a net), level up (a hollow), or (figuratively) to furnish (or imbue, diffuse, influence), satisfy, execute (an office), finish (a period or task), verify (or coincide with a prediction), etc.
Derivation: From G4134 (πλήρης).

e: which is put in to fill up, piece that filled up, fulfilling, full, fulness
d:
Repletion or completion, i.e. (subjectively) what fills (as contents, supplement, copiousness, multitude), or (objectively) what is filled (as container, performance, period).
Derivation: From G4137 (πληρόω).

(adverbially) close by; as noun, a neighbor, i.e. fellow (as man, countryman, Christian or friend).
Derivation: Neuter of a derivative of (near).

A filling up, i.e. (figuratively) gratification.
Derivation: From a presumed derivative of G4130 (πλήθω).

To pound, i.e. (figuratively) to inflict with (calamity).
Derivation: Apparently another form of G4111 (πλάσσω) (through the idea of flattening out).

A boat.
Derivation: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G4143 (πλοῖον).

A sailer, i.e. vessel.
Derivation: From G4126 (πλέω).

A sail, i.e. navigation.
Derivation: From G4126 (πλέω).

Wealthy; figuratively, abounding with.
Derivation: From G4149 (πλοῦτος).

Copiously.
Derivation: Adverb from G4145 (πλούσιος).

e: be increased with goods, (be made, wax) rich
d:
To be (or become) wealthy (literally or figuratively).
Derivation: From G4148 (πλουτίζω).

To make wealthy (figuratively).
Derivation: From G4149 (πλοῦτος).

Wealth (as fulness), i.e. (literally) money, possessions, or (figuratively) abundance, richness, (specially), valuable bestowment.
Derivation: From the base of G4130 (πλήθω).

To "plunge", i.e. launder clothing.
Derivation: A prolonged form of an obsolete (to "flow").

A current of air, i.e. breath (blast) or a breeze; by analogy or figuratively, a spirit, i.e. (human) the rational soul, (by implication) vital principle, mental disposition, etc., or (superhuman) an angel, demon, or (divine) God, Christ's spirit, the Holy Spirit.
Derivation: From G4154 (πνέω).

Non-carnal, i.e. (humanly) ethereal (as opposed to gross), or (dæmoniacally) a spirit (concretely), or (divinely) supernatural, regenerate, religious.
Derivation: From G4151 (πνεῦμα).

Non-physically, i.e. divinely, figuratively.
Derivation: Adverb from G4152 (πνευματικός).

To breathe hard, i.e. breeze.
Derivation: A primary word.

To wheeze, i.e. (causative, by implication) to throttle or strangle (drown).
Derivation: Strengthened from G4154 (πνέω).

Throttled, i.e. (neuter concretely) an animal choked to death (not bled).
Derivation: From G4155 (πνίγω).

Respiration, a breeze.
Derivation: From G4154 (πνέω).

A dress (G2066 (ἐσθής) implied) reaching the ankles.
Derivation: From G4228 (πούς) and another element of uncertain affinity.

From which (as interrogative) or what (as relative) place, state, source or cause.
Derivation: From the base of G4213 (πόσις) with enclitic adverb of origin.

e: abide, + agree, appoint, X avenge, + band together, be, bear, + bewray, bring (forth), ...
d:
To make or do (in a very wide application, more or less direct).
Derivation: Apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary.

A product, i.e. fabric (literally or figuratively).
Derivation: From G4160 (ποιέω).

Action, i.e. performance (of the law).
Derivation: From G4160 (ποιέω).

A performer; specially, a "poet".
Derivation: From G4160 (ποιέω).

Motley, i.e. various in character.
Derivation: Of uncertain derivation.

To tend as a shepherd of (figuratively, superviser).
Derivation: From G4166 (ποιμήν).

A shepherd (literally or figuratively).
Derivation: Of uncertain affinity.

A flock (literally or figuratively).
Derivation: Contraction from G4165 (ποιμαίνω).

A flock, i.e. (figuratively) group (of believers).
Derivation: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G4167 (ποίμνη).

Individualizing interrogative (of character) what sort of, or (of number) which one.

To be (engaged) in warfare, i.e. to battle (literally or figuratively).
Derivation: From G4171 (πόλεμος).

Warfare (literally or figuratively; a single encounter or a series).
Derivation: From (to bustle).

A town (properly, with walls, of greater or less size).
Derivation: Probably from the same as G4171 (πόλεμος), or perhaps from G4183 (πολύς).

A town-officer, i.e. magistrate.
Derivation: From G4172 (πόλις) and G757 (ἄρχω).

Citizenship; concretely, a community.
Derivation: From G4177 (πολίτης) ("polity").

A community, i.e. (abstractly) citizenship (figuratively).
Derivation: From G4176 (πολιτεύομαι).

To behave as a citizen (figuratively).
Derivation: Middle voice of a derivative of G4177 (πολίτης).

A townsman.
Derivation: From G4172 (πόλις).

Many times, i.e. frequently.
Derivation: Multiplicative adverb from G4183 (πολύς).

Manifold, i.e. (neuter as noun) very much more.
Derivation: From G4183 (πολύς) and probably a derivative of G4120 (πλέκω).

Loquacity, i.e. prolixity.
Derivation: From a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G3056 (λόγος).

In many portions, i.e. variously as to time and agency (piecemeal).
Derivation: Adverb from a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G3313 (μέρος).

Much variegated, i.e. multifarious.
Derivation: From G4183 (πολύς) and G4164 (ποικίλος).

e: abundant, + altogether, common, + far (passed, spent), (+ be of a) great (age, deal, -ly, ...
d:
(singular) much (in any respect) or (plural) many; neuter (singular) as adverbial, largely; neuter (plural) as adverb or noun often, mostly, largely.
Derivation: Including the forms from the alternate.

Extremely compassionate.
Derivation: From G4183 (πολύς) and G4698 (σπλάγχνον) (figuratively).

e: costly, very precious, of great price
d:
Extremely expensive.
Derivation: From G4183 (πολύς) and G5056 (τέλος).

Extremely valuable.
Derivation: From G4183 (πολύς) and G5092 (τιμή).

In many ways, i.e. variously as to method or form.
Derivation: Adverb from a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G5158 (τρόπος).

A beverage.
Derivation: From the alternate of G4095 (πίνω).

Depravity, i.e. (specially), malice; plural (concretely) plots, sins.
Derivation: From G4190 (πονηρός).

d:
Hurtful, i.e. evil (properly, in effect or influence, and thus differing from G2556 (κακός), which refers rather to essential character, as well as from G4550 (σαπρός), which indicates degeneracy from original virtue); figuratively, calamitous; also (passively) ill, i.e. diseased; but especially (morally) culpable, i.e. derelict, vicious, facinorous; neuter (singular) mischief, malice, or (plural) guilt; masculine (singular) the devil, or (plural) sinners.
Derivation: From a derivative of G4192 (πόνος).

More evil.
Derivation: Comparative of G4190 (πονηρός).

Toil, i.e. (by implication) anguish.
Derivation: From the base of G3993 (πένης).

A Pontican, i.e. native of Pontus.
Derivation: From G4195 (Πόντος).

Apparently bridged; Pontius, a Roman.
Derivation: Of Latin origin.

A sea; Pontus, a region of Asia Minor.
Derivation: Of Latin origin.

Apparently "popular"; Poplius (i.e. Publius), a Roman.
Derivation: Of Latin origin.

Travel (by land); figuratively (plural) proceedings, i.e. career.
Derivation: From G4198 (πορεύομαι).

e: depart, go (away, forth, one's way, up), (make a, take a) journey, walk
d:
To traverse, i.e. travel (literally or figuratively; especially to remove (figuratively, die), live, etc.).
Derivation: Middle voice from a derivative of the same as G3984 (πεῖρα).

To ravage (figuratively).
Derivation: Prolongation from (to sack).

Furnishing (procuring), i.e. (by implication) money-getting (acquisition).
Derivation: From a derivative of (a way, i.e. means).

Apparently swinish; Porcius, a Roman.
Derivation: Of Latin origin.

Harlotry (including adultery and incest); figuratively, idolatry.
Derivation: From G4203 (πορνεύω).

To act the harlot, i.e. (literally) indulge unlawful lust (of either sex), or (figuratively) practise idolatry.
Derivation: From G4204 (πόρνη).

A strumpet; figuratively, an idolater.
Derivation: Feminine of G4205 (πόρνος).

Akin to the base of G4097 (πιπράσκω)); a (male) prostitute (as venal), i.e. (by analogy) a debauchee (libertine).
Derivation: From (to sell.

Forwards, i.e. at a distance.

From far, or (by implication) at a distance, i.e. distantly.
Derivation: From G4206 (πόῤῥω) with adverbial enclitic of source.

Further, i.e. a greater distance.
Derivation: Adverb comparative of G4206 (πόῤῥω).

The "purple" mussel, i.e. (by implication) the red-blue color itself, and finally a garment dyed with it.
Derivation: Of Latin origin.

Purpureal, i.e. bluish red.
Derivation: From G4209 (πορφύρα).

A female trader in purple cloth.
Derivation: Feminine of a compound of G4209 (πορφύρα) and G4453 (πωλέω).

How many times.
Derivation: Multiplicative from G4214 (πόσος).

A drinking (the act), i.e. (concretely) a draught.
Derivation: From the alternate of G4095 (πίνω).

Interrogative pronoun (of amount) how much (large, long or (plural) many).
Derivation: From an absolute (who, what) and G3739 (ὅς).

A current, brook or freshet (as drinkable), i.e. running water.
Derivation: Probably from a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω) (compare G4224 (πότος)).

River-borne, i.e. overwhelmed by a stream.
Derivation: From G4215 (ποταμός) and a derivative of G5409 (φορέω).

Interrogatively, whatever, i.e. of what possible sort.
Derivation: Apparently from G4219 (πότε) and the base of G4226 (ποῦ).

e: afore-(any, some-)time(-s), at length (the last), (+ n- )ever, in the old time, ...
d:
Indefinite adverb, at some time, ever.
Derivation: From the base of G4225 (πού) and G5037 (τέ).

Interrogative adverb, at what time.
Derivation: From the base of G4226 (ποῦ) and G5037 (τέ).

Interrogative as adverb, which (of two), i.e. is it this or that.
Derivation: Neuter of a comparative of the base of G4226 (ποῦ).

A drinking-vessel; by extension, the contents thereof, i.e. a cupful (draught); figuratively, a lot or fate.
Derivation: Neuter of a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω).

To furnish drink, irrigate.
Derivation: From a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω).

Little wells, i.e. mineral springs; Potioli (i.e. Puteoli), a place in Italy.
Derivation: Of Latin origin.

A drinking-bout or carousal.
Derivation: From the alternate of G4095 (πίνω).

As adverb of place, somewhere, i.e. nearly.
Derivation: Genitive case of an indefinite pronoun (some) otherwise obsolete (compare G4214 (πόσος)).

As adverb of place; at (by implication, to) what locality.
Derivation: Genitive case of an interrogative pronoun (what) otherwise obsolete (perhaps the same as G4225 (πού) used with the rising slide of inquiry).

Modest; Pudes (i.e. Pudens), a Christian.
Derivation: Of Latin origin.

A "foot" (figuratively or literally).
Derivation: A primary word.

A deed; by implication, an affair; by extension, an object (material).
Derivation: From G4238 (πράσσω).

A transaction, i.e. negotiation.
Derivation: From G4231 (πραγματεύομαι).

To busy oneself with, i.e. to trade.
Derivation: From G4229 (πρᾶγμα).

The prætorium or governor's courtroom (sometimes including the whole edifice and camp).
Derivation: Of Latin origin.

A practiser, i.e. (specially), an official collector.
Derivation: From a derivative of G4238 (πράσσω).

Practice, i.e. (concretely) an act; by extension, a function.
Derivation: From G4238 (πράσσω).

Gentle, i.e. humble.
Derivation: A form of G4239 (πραΰς), used in certain parts.

Gentleness, by implication, humility.
Derivation: From G4235 (πρᾷος).

A garden plot, i.e. (by implication, of regular beds) a row (repeated in plural by Hebraism, to indicate an arrangement).

e: commit, deeds, do, exact, keep, require, use arts
d:
To "practise", i.e. perform repeatedly or habitually (thus differing from G4160 (ποιέω), which properly refers to a single act); by implication, to execute, accomplish, etc.; specially, to collect (dues), fare (personally).
Derivation: A primary verb.

Mild, i.e. (by implication) humble.
Derivation: Apparently a primary word.

Mildness, i.e. (by implication) humility.
Derivation: From G4239 (πραΰς).

To tower up (be conspicuous), i.e. (by implication) to be suitable or proper (third person singular present indicative, often used impersonally, it is fit or right).
Derivation: Apparently a primary verb.

Seniority (eldership), i.e. (by implication) an embassy (concretely, ambassadors).
Derivation: From G4243 (πρεσβεύω).

To be a senior, i.e. (by implication) act as a representative (figuratively, preacher).
Derivation: From the base of G4245 (πρεσβύτερος).

The order of elders, i.e. (specially), Israelite Sanhedrin or Christian "presbytery".
Derivation: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G4245 (πρεσβύτερος).

Older; as noun, a senior; specially, an Israelite Sanhedrist (also figuratively, member of the celestial council) or Christian "presbyter".
Derivation: Comparative of (elderly).

An old man.
Derivation: From the same as G4245 (πρεσβύτερος).

An old woman.
Derivation: Feminine of G4246 (πρεσβύτης).

Leaning (falling) forward ("prone"), i.e. head foremost.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό).

To saw in two.
Derivation: A strengthened form of a primary prio (to saw).

Prior, sooner.
Derivation: Adverb from G4253 (πρό).

Feminine of Priscus, ancient; Priska, a Christian woman.
Derivation: Of Latin origin.

Priscilla (i.e. little Prisca), a Christian woman.
Derivation: Diminutive of G4251 (Πρίσκα).

"fore", i.e. in front of, prior (figuratively, superior) to.
Derivation: A primary preposition.

To lead forward (magisterially); intransitively, to precede (in place or time (participle, previous)).
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G71 (ἄγω).

To choose for oneself before another thing (prefer), i.e. (by implication) to propose (intend).
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G138 (αἱρέομαι).

To accuse already, i.e. previously charge.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G156 (αἰτία).

To hear already,i.e. anticipate.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G191 (ἀκούω).

To sin previously (to conversion).
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G264 (ἁμαρτάνω).

A forecourt, i.e. vestibule (alley-way).
Derivation: Neuter of a presumed compound of G4253 (πρό) and G833 (αὐλή).

e: + be of a great age, go farther (on), be well stricken
d:
To walk forward, i.e. advance (literally, or in years).
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and the base of G939 (βάσις).

To throw forward, i.e. push to the front, germinate.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G906 (βάλλω).

Relating to sheep, i.e. (a gate) through which they were led into Jerusalem.
Derivation: From G4263 (πρόβατον).

Something that walks forward (a quadruped), i.e. (specially), a sheep (literally or figuratively).
Derivation: Probably neuter of a presumed derivative of G4260 (προβαίνω).

To force forward, i.e. bring to the front, instigate.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and a reduplicated form of G971 (βιάζω).

To look out beforehand, i.e. furnish in advance.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G991 (βλέπω).

To be already, i.e. have previousy transpired.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G1096 (γίνομαι).

To know beforehand, i.e. foresee.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G1097 (γινώσκω).

Forethought.
Derivation: From G4267 (προγινώσκω).

An ancestor, (grand-)parent.
Derivation: From G4266 (προγίνομαι).

e: before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore, aforetime)
d:
To write previously; figuratively, to announce, prescribe.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G1125 (γράφω).

Plain before all men, i.e. obvious.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G1212 (δῆλος).

To give before the other party has given.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G1325 (δίδωμι).

A surrender.
Derivation: From G4272 (προδίδωμι) (in the sense of giving forward into another's (the enemy's) hands).

A runner ahead, i.e. scout (figuratively, precursor).
Derivation: From the alternate of G4390 (προτρέχω).

Foresee.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G1492 (εἴδω).

To hope in advance of other confirmation.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G1679 (ἐλπίζω).

To say already, to predict.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2036 (ἔπω).

To commence already.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G1728 (ἐνάρχομαι).

To promise of old.
Derivation: Middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G1861 (ἐπαγγέλλω).

Used as alternate of G4277 (προέπω); to say already, predict.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2046 (ἐρέω).

e: go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on
d:
To go onward, precede (in place or time).
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι) (including its alternate).

To fit up in advance (literally or figuratively).
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2090 (ἑτοιμάζω).

To announce glad news in advance.
Derivation: Middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2097 (εὐαγγελίζω).

To hold oneself before others, i.e. (figuratively) to excel.
Derivation: Middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2192 (ἔχω).

To lead the way for others, i.e. show deference.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2233 (ἡγέομαι).

A setting forth, i.e. (figuratively) proposal (intention); specially, the show-bread (in the Temple) as exposed before God.
Derivation: From G4388 (προτίθεμαι).

Fixed beforehand, i.e. (feminine with G2250 (ἡμέρα) implied) a designated day.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι).

e: forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind
d:
Predisposition, i.e. alacrity.
Derivation: From G4289 (πρόθυμος).

Forward in spirit, i.e. predisposed; neuter (as noun) alacrity.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2372 (θυμός).

With alacrity.
Derivation: Adverb from G4289 (πρόθυμος).

To stand before, i.e. (in rank) to preside, or (by implication) to practise.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2476 (ἵστημι).

To call forth to oneself (challenge), i.e. (by implication) to irritate.
Derivation: Middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2564 (καλέω).

To anounce beforehand, i.e. predict, promise.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2605 (καταγγέλλω).

To prepare in advance.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2675 (καταρτίζω).

To lie before the view, i.e. (figuratively) to be present (to the mind), to stand forth (as an example or reward).
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2749 (κεῖμαι).

To herald (i.e. proclaim) in advance.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2784 (κηρύσσω).

Progress, i.e. advancement (subjectively or objectively).
Derivation: From G4298 (προκόπτω).

e: increase, proceed, profit, be far spent, wax
d:
To drive forward (as if by beating), i.e. (figuratively and intransitively) to advance (in amount, to grow; in time, to be well along).
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2875 (κόπτω).

A prejudgment (prejudice), i.e. prepossession.
Derivation: From a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G2919 (κρίνω).

To ratify previously.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2964 (κυρόω).

To take in advance, i.e. (literally) eat before others have an opportunity; (figuratively) to anticipate, surprise.
Derivation: From G4253 (πρό) and G2983 (λαμβάνω).
